# Example config

A fully commented `config.toml`, generated from the same defaults as the configuration reference. [Download it](baud.toml) and uncomment what you want to change.

```toml
# Every option at its default, commented out. Uncomment and edit any
# line to override it. Generated by `cargo run --bin docs-gen`; options
# with no default shown here are unset in Config::default() (there is no
# literal TOML value for "unset") — see the configuration reference for
# their behavior when set.

# Allows the running program to read the clipboard via OSC 52; disable if you do not trust every program you run interactively.
# allow_osc52_read = false
# Maps SGR bold text to the bright variant of its ANSI color. Equivalent to `[theme].bold_is_bright`, and OR'd with it: either one being true enables the mapping.
# bold_is_bright = false

[copy_mode]
# Enables copy mode, letting its keybinding (Ctrl+Shift+X by default) take effect.
# enabled = true

[cursor]
# Makes the cursor blink, independently of SGR 5 blinking text.
# blink = true
# Blink interval in milliseconds, shared by the cursor and SGR 5 blinking text. `0` disables both: the cursor stays solid and blinking text stays visible.
# blink_interval_ms = 530
# Cursor shape: "block", "bar", or "underline".
# style = "block"

[debug]
# Allows the FPS counter overlay to be toggled with its keybinding.
# fps_counter_enabled = false

[diagnostics]
# Measures key-to-presentation latency (from `KeyboardInput` to `frame.present()`), logging p50/p95/p99 every 60 samples. This is a strict lower bound: it excludes keyboard, compositor, and panel latency.
# latency_probe = false
# Runs a background thread that detects an unresponsive event loop. Requires a restart to take effect.
# watchdog = false

[font]
# Draws box-drawing (U+2500-U+259F) and Powerline separator (U+E0B0-U+E0B3) glyphs procedurally instead of relying on the font to include them.
# builtin_box_drawing = true
# Fallback font families tried in order when the primary family is missing a glyph, such as emoji, CJK, or symbol fonts.
# fallback = []
# Font family name, resolved through fontdb. Defaults to a Nerd Font on Linux and Cascadia Mono on Windows, so box-drawing and Powerline glyphs render without extra setup.
# family = "FiraCode Nerd Font Mono"
# Enables multi-character ligature shaping. Off by default, since ligatures can visually merge adjacent operators in code.
# ligatures = false
# Line height multiplier applied to the cell grid.
# line_height = 1.0
# Font size in points.
# size = 12

[font.glyph_offset]
# Fine horizontal pixel offset applied to every glyph within its cell, for fonts whose glyphs need nudging.
# x = 0.0
# Fine vertical pixel offset applied to every glyph within its cell, for fonts whose baseline needs nudging.
# y = 0.0

[notifications]
# Shows a desktop notification when the running program emits OSC 9 or OSC 777.
# enabled = false

[panes]
# Maximum number of panes per tab. `0` means no limit.
# max = 12
# Keeps each pane's split orientation fixed across resizes instead of recalculating it. `smart_split` implies this as well.
# preserve_split = false
# Chooses a new split's orientation from where the mouse is within the pane, like Hyprland's dwindle triangles, instead of always splitting the long axis.
# smart_split = false
# Hyprland-style `split_width_multiplier`: biases new splits wider or narrower than an even half.
# split_width_multiplier = 1.0

[process]
# Extra arguments passed to the shell on launch.
# args = []
# Session backend: "native" for the platform's own shell, or "wsl" to run inside a WSL distribution (Windows only).
# kind = "native"
# Launches the shell as a login shell.
# login = false

[render]
# Synchronize presentation with the monitor refresh rate. Disabling it lowers input latency at the cost of possible tearing.
# vsync = true

[scrollback]
# Synthetic arrow-key presses sent per mouse wheel tick while an alternate-screen application, such as a pager or editor, owns the scrolling.
# faux_multiplier = 3.0
# Maximum number of scrollback lines retained. `0` keeps no history at all.
# lines = 10000
# Lines scrolled per mouse wheel tick while browsing normal-screen scrollback.
# multiplier = 3.0
# Ignores `scrollback.lines` and keeps every line for the life of the session.
# unlimited = false

[selection]
# Modifier keys that suppress the running program's own mouse reporting so Baud's selection takes over instead, even in mouse-aware apps like vim or tmux.
# bypass_mouse_reporting_modifiers = ["shift"]
# Copies the selection to the clipboard automatically when the left mouse button is released.
# copy_on_select = false
# Delay after releasing the mouse button before copy-on-select fires, so a click that is about to extend into a drag is not copied prematurely.
# copy_on_select_delay_ms = 500
# Clipboard destination for copy-on-select: "primary", "clipboard", or "both".
# copy_on_select_target = "both"
# Expands a double-click to a whole URL, path, or email address instead of stopping at the nearest delimiter.
# smart_selection = true
# Characters treated as word boundaries for a non-smart double-click selection.
# word_delimiters = """,│`|:"' ()[]{}<>\t"""

[status]
# How long the status overlay stays visible before it auto-dismisses. `0` disables the automatic dismiss.
# duration_ms = 2000

[theme]
# Terminal background color, and the color the window clears to before each frame.
# background = "#0a0a0a"
# ANSI color 0 (SGR 30/40) and its background counterpart.
# black = "#3d3d3d"
# ANSI color 4 (SGR 34/44) and its background counterpart.
# blue = "#6b9fd4"
# Maps SGR bold text to the bright variant of its ANSI color. Same switch as the root-level `bold_is_bright`, OR'd together with it.
# bold_is_bright = false
# ANSI color 8 (SGR 90/100), the bright variant of black; also used as the comment/dim reference color.
# bright_black = "#797979"
# ANSI color 12 (SGR 94/104), the bright variant of blue.
# bright_blue = "#82b4e8"
# ANSI color 14 (SGR 96/106), the bright variant of cyan.
# bright_cyan = "#72d0d0"
# ANSI color 10 (SGR 92/102), the bright variant of green.
# bright_green = "#7ed49a"
# ANSI color 13 (SGR 95/105), the bright variant of magenta.
# bright_magenta = "#d494e8"
# ANSI color 9 (SGR 91/101), the bright variant of red.
# bright_red = "#f07070"
# ANSI color 15 (SGR 97/107), the bright variant of white.
# bright_white = "#ffffff"
# ANSI color 11 (SGR 93/103), the bright variant of yellow.
# bright_yellow = "#e8b888"
# Fallback cursor color, used unless `[cursor].color` overrides it.
# cursor = "#d97757"
# ANSI color 6 (SGR 36/46) and its background counterpart.
# cyan = "#5eb8b8"
# Renders SGR dim by fading the glyph's alpha instead of darkening its RGB color.
# dim_alpha = false
# Default text color, used wherever a cell has no explicit SGR foreground.
# foreground = "#ececec"
# ANSI color 2 (SGR 32/42) and its background counterpart.
# green = "#6bbf8a"
# ANSI color 5 (SGR 35/45) and its background counterpart.
# magenta = "#c47ad4"
# Minimum WCAG contrast ratio enforced between foreground and effective background per cell. `1.0` disables the adjustment and keeps raw theme colors; `3.0` is the large-text floor; `4.5` matches WCAG AA body text.
# minimum_contrast = 1.0
# ANSI color 1 (SGR 31/41) and its background counterpart.
# red = "#e85d5d"
# Background color of selected text. Unset falls back to a semi-transparent `theme.black`.
# selection_bg = "#c4704a"
# Foreground color of selected text.
# selection_fg = "#0a0a0a"
# ANSI color 7 (SGR 37/47) and its background counterpart.
# white = "#ececec"
# ANSI color 3 (SGR 33/43) and its background counterpart.
# yellow = "#d4a574"

[window]
# Window decorations: "system" uses the native title bar, "custom" draws Baud's unified title bar with inline tabs and window controls, and "none" removes decorations entirely. The previous boolean values still work: true maps to "system" and false to "none".
# decorations = "system"
# Initial window height in logical pixels. Only applies when `startup` is "windowed".
# height = 600
# Window opacity from 0 to 1. Values below 1 let the desktop show through the background wherever the GPU backend supports transparency.
# opacity = 1.0
# Extra horizontal pixels of blank space between the window edge and the terminal grid.
# padding_x = 0
# Extra vertical pixels of blank space between the window edge and the terminal grid.
# padding_y = 0
# Initial window state: "windowed", "maximized", or "fullscreen".
# startup = "windowed"
# Initial window width in logical pixels. Only applies when `startup` is "windowed".
# width = 800

```
